subject: Pilot billing: sparse inference patterns and burst-crediting clarification
messages:
From: Alex Harper <alex.harper@retailco.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ryan Cole <ryan.cole@retailco.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify billing for sparse inference patterns (pilot)

Hi Rohan,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. We want to kick off the 60-day pilot next week but need one last clarification on how billing will behave for our workload. A few specifics:

- Most inference calls are extremely short (50-150 tokens) and very sparse (avg 3 calls/minute per endpoint), but we have occasional 30s microbursts during campaigns (up to ~800 concurrent calls).
- We rely heavily on prefix reuse across customers (lots of identical prompts where KV cache should help).

Questions:
1) Do you charge a minimum per-call token quantum (e.g., 1-minute aggregation or X token floor) for streaming/generation requests?
2) If a burst happens, does Redwood attempt to aggregate/round to an hourly or per-minute window for billing, or are those bursts billed individually?
3) How does prefix/KV reuse factor into billed tokens — is there an explicit credit for reuse or is it implicitly lower tokens when hits occur?

We attached a small sample of our synthetic traffic to illustrate distribution.

Also, on pricing: our procurement team needs an explicit pilot concession (discount and possible waive of minimums) to sign the PO. Can you confirm what's feasible?

Best,
Alex
Alex Harper
Head of ML Integrations, RetailCo
[Attachment: retailco_usage_sample.csv (text/csv)]

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Harper <alex.harper@retailco.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify billing for sparse inference patterns (pilot)

Hi Alex — thanks for the sample and clear questions. Looping in Kim (pricing) and Sergio (platform) to make sure we cover implementation details. High-level answers first, then a proposed pilot concession.

1) Minimums/quantum: Our hosted billing engine uses a 60-second aggregation window for per-call streaming/generation by default to avoid charging for tiny sub-second calls individually. That means calls within the same 60s window for the same API key + model are aggregated for billing quantum, subject to our session bucketing rules. There is also a per-minute floor when the call would otherwise fall under the subtoken rounding threshold.

2) Bursts: Bursts are billed against the same aggregation windows; however, in the absence of a committed volume, they appear as on-demand usage and may push you into higher slab pricing if sustained. For pilot customers we can enable a microburst-crediting feature: we create a per-month buffer of burst tokens (configurable) that will be netted against on-demand spikes before computing overage. For example, a 5% burst buffer on a 1M token monthly commit would absorb 50k tokens of spikes without moving you to next slab.

3) Prefix/KV reuse: Billing is per-generated/consumed token. That said, when KV cache hits occur, the runtime avoids re-computation which reduces emitted tokens and thus reduces charged tokens. We do not currently provide an explicit separate "KV credit" line item — it's reflected in lower token counts on your invoice. We can export per-prefix hit rates in daily usage CSVs for transparency.

Proposed pilot concession (subject to SOW language):
- 30-day pilot: waive the 60s minimum for the first 30 days for endpoints participating in the pilot (i.e., no per-minute floor for those calls)
- 20% off per-token rates for the pilot period
- Enable a 5% monthly burst buffer for the length of the pilot (netted before slab computation)

Attaching a brief invoice stub showing expected mapping of your sample traffic to billable tokens with the concession applied. If procurement needs a stronger discount, we can discuss a short-term uplift in committed monthly tokens in exchange for a deeper concession.

Next steps: if this looks acceptable I can have contracts draft a SOW and Sergio will provision the monitoring/export hook for prefix hit rates.

Thanks,
Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pilot_invoice_stub.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Alex Harper <alex.harper@retailco.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ryan Cole <ryan.cole@retailco.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@retailco.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify billing for sparse inference patterns (pilot)

Rohan — appreciate the quick answers and the invoice stub. Two asks from our side before the PO:

- For commercial reasons we need a stronger safety net for bursts during initial campaigns. Can Redwood increase the burst buffer to 10% for the first 60 days? Alternatively, we can commit to a small reserved capacity (e.g., 250K tokens/month) if that gets us a deeper discount.
- Procurement has asked for a 30% discount for the first 90 days to offset integration and parallel-run costs.

If you can accommodate either (10% burst buffer for 60 days + current 20% discount) or (5% burst buffer + 30% discount with a 250K token reserved commit), we can sign quickly. Also confirm you will provide the per-prefix hit-rate daily export (CSV) and a shared dashboard so we can track effective savings.

Can we set a short call tomorrow to finalize details?

Thanks,
Alex

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Harper <alex.harper@retailco.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify billing for sparse inference patterns (pilot)

Alex — thanks, and understood on both asks. Quick summary and what we can commit to: 

- Burst buffer: we can temporarily increase the burst buffer to 10% for the first 60 days for the pilot endpoints. That will be active as soon as SOW is signed and Sergio confirms the endpoints to protect.
- Discounting: we can offer 25% off per-token rates for the first 90 days if RetailCo agrees to a 250K token/month committed tranche for the same 90-day period (the commit buys a lower long-run unit price and lets us reserve capacity). The alternative (no commit + 30% for 90d) isn't something we can sustain across accounts, but 25% + 250K commit is achievable.

Operational commitments:
- We will provide a daily CSV export with per-prefix hit rate and token counts (Sergio will enable feeds).
- Transactions will remain mapped to the 60s aggregation windows for reconciliation, but pilot endpoints will be exempt from the per-minute floor for the first 30 days as previously noted.
- Contracts will draft an amendment capturing the 250K/token monthly commit and the 25% pilot discount. Please route the PO to procurement@retailco.com and copy me.

If that works, I'll schedule a 30-min alignment call (Kim can join for pricing) and have legal spin a redline. Proposed times: Thu 10:00–10:30 PT or Thu 14:00–14:30 PT.

Cheers,
Rohan
